incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: autoscaler.queue_len_high for svc=serve-prod us-west-2 (threshold 500)
incident-bot: metric snapshot: queue_length=1423, inflight=128, processing_rate=60r/s, enqueue_rate=210r/s, avg_latency=12.4s
pagerduty: Paging jordan (oncall) for high-priority incident (INC-2026-1123)
jordan (oncall): acked. I'm on it. Starting triage — checking autoscaler controller logs and cluster node metrics.
mike: saw the alert, adding context: burst from batch-inference job in customer-X org started ~10m ago, looks like many long-running requests.
anya: @jordan FYI, we rolled a config change to autoscaler last week (queue-smoothing window tweak). might be related.
chen: quick check: control-plane shows no new node launches in the last 8m despite increased pending pods. kube-controller logs show scaling decisions but failing due to quota error: 
```
E0423 03:02:14 scaler.go:142] scale failed: insufficient capacity in nodepool-prod-usw2 (requested 4 nodes, available 0), cloud error: QuotaExceeded
```
chen: looks like cloud quota exhausted in us-west-2 nodepool.
jordan (oncall): ok — autoscaler is healthy but cloud quota prevented scale out. That explains backlog. Assessing customer impact: per logs ~3% 503s, 18% tail latency >5s for text-generation endpoints. Worthy of page.
mike: workaround options: 1) temporarily route new requests to us-east-1, 2) force-scale nodepool to different instance type, 3) spin up dedicated burst pool in another nodepool if allowed.
anya: can we enable model-fallback to a smaller quantized variant to reduce processing time? RDW has a v2q variant available for serve-prod. Would reduce CPU/GPU time per request.
jordan (oncall): starting mitigation: 1) open PD incident notes, 2) put canary route to us-east-1 for non-PCI traffic, 3) trigger manual scale for nodepool-other-region, 4) enable fallback policy for heavy endpoints. Executing now.
jordan (oncall): runbook command to enable fallback: 
```
# enable fallback route for model svc
redwoodctl routes set-fallback --service serve-prod --variant v2q --percent 40
```
jordan (oncall): ran redwoodctl, fallback enabled to 40% traffic. monitoring for latency.
chen: manual scale command to other nodepool: 
```
gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize nodepool-east-ig --size=20 --region=us-east1
```
chen: triggered. cloud accepted new instances, nodes starting.
incident-bot: automatic notification: route-change deployed, nodepool-east scaling event kicked off.
mike: after fallback and east scaling, queue_length dropped from 1423 -> 420 over 4m, processing_rate up to 160r/s. Tail latency improving.
jordan (oncall): good. I'm going to pause autoscaler config rollout (the smoothing change) and open a rollback PR — not running risky changes during incidents.
anya: I've posted a short customer-outage blurb in #support to prepare CS: "We'll see intermittent high latency for text-gen endpoints in us-west-2, traffic shifted to other regions while we add capacity."
sre-shift-lead: nice work. action items: (1) follow up with infra to request emergency quota increase in us-west-2, (2) create postmortem if quota change or rollout caused this, (3) ensure autoscaler failsafe is added to detect quota errors and trigger cross-region fallback automatically.
jordan (oncall): handing off to mike for monitoring and follow-ups; I'll create the incident page and start timeline. @mike you own the watch for 1h and then hand to night oncall.
mike: taking over. I'll watch queue and latency, will post updates every 10m. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: system note: incident INC-2026-1123 created and linked to this thread.
pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by jordan (oncall). Escalation suppressed.
mike: 10m update — queue_length=220, processing_rate=155r/s, error_rate down to 0.6%, tail latency 1.2s. No new customer-facing 503s observed.
mike: 30m update — queue steady ~80, autoscaler still paused for rollout, nodepool-east at target capacity, fallback remains 40%. I'm going to reduce fallback to 20% in 15m if stable.
anya: created follow-up ticket INFRA-2314: "Quota exhaustion caused autoscaler stall — emergency quota request + autoscaler failsafe". Assigned to chen and infra team.
chen: noted. I'll coordinate with cloud provider for quota increase and confirm timelines.
jordan (oncall): final note before handoff — we mitigated customer impact with cross-region routing and model fallback. Root cause likely twofold: cloud quota reached + aggressive autoscaler smoothing from last rollout. Creating a full postmortem. Handoff to mike at 1774511200 for monitoring and next steps.
mike: acked handoff, on watch. I'll update incident channel if anything changes and escalate to oncall again if queue >300 or error_rate >2%.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated, monitoring.
